[Kopia](https://kopia.io/) makes encrypted, deduplicated snapshots of your
files to a disk, a NAS or a cloud storage. This integration brings the sources
of a Kopia server into Gladys: each source (a folder backed up) becomes a
device with its state, its last successful snapshot, its size, its files and
the errors of its last snapshot. Scenes can react when **any** snapshot
succeeds, fails or is overdue (no success for too long), a dashboard widget
lists the failed sources first, and a scene can start a snapshot.

Tested against a real Kopia 0.23 (Docker image `kopia/kopia`, filesystem
repository, Basic authentication, HTTP and self-signed HTTPS): a snapshot that
succeeds, one with a file it cannot read, one whose folder was deleted, and a
snapshot started from the integration. Not yet tested on a real Gladys:
feedback welcome on [the issues](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-kopia/issues).

## What you need

- Gladys Assistant 5.1.0 or later.
- Kopia running as a **server** with its web interface, `kopia server start`,
  reachable from the Gladys machine (port 51515 by default). KopiaUI, the
  desktop application, only listens to its own computer: it cannot be used.
- The username and the password of the server, given with
  `--server-username` (`kopia` by default) and `--server-password`. Not the
  password of the repository.

The integration reads Kopia every 5 minutes by default (every 30 seconds while
a snapshot runs): a handful of light requests on your own network.

## Getting started

### 1. Start the Kopia server

For example, with a certificate generated by Kopia:

```
kopia server start --address=0.0.0.0:51515 \
  --server-username=kopia --server-password=… \
  --tls-generate-cert
```

At the first start, Kopia shows `SERVER CERT SHA256: …`: note this
fingerprint. With `--insecure` instead of a certificate, the server speaks
plain HTTP: use it only on a network you trust. The Docker image `kopia/kopia`
takes the same options.

### 2. Configure the integration

In Gladys, **Integrations → Kopia → Configuration**:

- **Kopia address**: `https://192.168.1.2:51515` for example (`http://` with
  `--insecure`). A bare address (`192.168.1.2`) means `http://` on port 51515;
  an address copied from the browser works too.
- **Username** and **Password**: the `--server-username` and
  `--server-password` of the server.
- **Certificate fingerprint**: only for a self-signed certificate
  (`--tls-generate-cert`): the `SERVER CERT SHA256` noted above. The
  integration then accepts this certificate, and no other, always over `https://`. Leave it empty with
  `http://` or a certificate signed by a known authority.
- **Refresh interval**: 1, 5 (default) or 15 minutes.
- **Overdue after**: when a source without a successful snapshot becomes
  overdue. _Automatic_ (default) follows the scheduling policy of each source:
  its interval plus a quarter of it (an hour at least) — 30 hours for a daily
  snapshot, also for "times of day". A source without interval (manual, or a
  cron expression) is then never overdue. Or a fixed delay, from 12 hours to a
  week, for every source.
- **Allow starting snapshots**: lets the scene action "Start a snapshot" work.
  Disable it if nobody should start a snapshot from Gladys.
- **Language of the names**: language of the feature names, of the states and
  of the scene results.

**Test the connection** reads Kopia and sums up: the number of sources, failed
and overdue.

### 3. Add the sources

In the **Discover** tab, add the sources to follow, and the "Kopia" device for
the server. A source appears once it has a policy or a snapshot in Kopia.
Scene triggers work for every source, added or not.

## The devices

Each source:

| Feature                     | Value                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| State                       | OK, Failed, Overdue, Running or No snapshot            |
| Last successful snapshot    | day/month hours:minutes, "-" if none                   |
| Hours since last success    | in hours                                               |
| Last snapshot duration      | in seconds                                             |
| Size                        | size of the files of the last snapshot, in MB          |
| Files                       | files of the last snapshot                             |
| Snapshots                   | snapshots kept in the repository                       |
| Errors of the last snapshot | files it could not read (1 for a snapshot that failed) |
| Running                     | 1 while a snapshot of this source runs                 |
| Next scheduled snapshot     | day/month hours:minutes, "-" without schedule          |

The "Kopia" device, for the server:

- **Repository connected**: 1, or 0 when the server is not connected to its
  repository;
- **Snapshot running**: 1 or 0;
- **Progress**: in %;
- **Current source**: its path, "-" if none;
- **Failed sources** and **Overdue sources**: how many.

A snapshot "fails" when Kopia could not read some files (it saves the
snapshot without them), when it is incomplete, or when it fails completely (a
folder deleted, a storage unreachable: no snapshot is saved). The errors the
policy of the source ignores do not count. The state shows what needs
attention first: a failed source shows "Failed" even when it is also overdue.

The sources of another computer or user (clients of the same repository) are
named `user@host:/path`.

## Dashboard

The **Kopia** widget shows the number of sources failed, overdue and OK, then
one row per source: failed first, then overdue, running, without snapshot, OK,
with the last success (or the progress of the one running). Every source by
default, or the ones chosen in its settings. The **Refresh** button reads
Kopia again.

## Scenes

### Triggers

- **A snapshot succeeds**: a snapshot completes without error. Information:
  source, duration (minutes), files, size, snapshots kept.
- **A snapshot fails**: files unreadable, an incomplete snapshot, or a complete
  failure. Information: source, first error, errors.
- **A source is overdue**: a source has had no successful snapshot for longer
  than the "Overdue after" delay. Once per delay exceeded, again after a new
  success. Information: source, hours since last success, last success.

Each trigger can be limited to some sources (empty: any).

### Actions

- **State of a source**: reads the state of a source for the next actions:
  failed, overdue, the state in words, the source, the last success, hours
  since last success (-1 if none), and a ready-made sentence ("/home/anna:
  Failed, last success 18/10 02:05.").
- **Start a snapshot**: starts a snapshot of the source now. Refused when
  "Allow starting snapshots" is disabled.

### Scene ideas

- **A snapshot fails** → send a message with the source and its first error,
  picked from the information of the trigger.
- **A source is overdue** → notify with the source and the hours since its
  last success.
- Every Sunday at 10:00 → **State of a source** → send the sentence; or start
  a snapshot of the photos when you leave home, with **Start a snapshot**.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Kopia does not answer"**: check the address and the port from the Gladys
  machine, and that the server listens to the network
  (`--address=0.0.0.0:51515`, not `127.0.0.1`).
- **"username or password refused by Kopia"**: type them again; they are the
  ones of `--server-username` and `--server-password`.
- **"certificate refused"**: a self-signed certificate; enter its fingerprint
  in the configuration.
- **"the certificate does not match the fingerprint"**: the certificate
  changed (Kopia generates a new one when its files are deleted): enter the new
  fingerprint.
- **"Kopia is not connected to its repository"**: connect the server to its
  repository again in its web interface.
- **A source never becomes overdue**: in _Automatic_, a source without
  interval cannot be overdue; choose a fixed delay. A source that never
  succeeded is not overdue either: it shows Failed or No snapshot.
- **A complete failure is no longer shown after Kopia restarted**: Kopia keeps
  its tasks in memory only; the integration still announced it when it
  happened.
- To see more, set the `LOG_LEVEL` variable of the integration to `debug`.

## Limits

- One Kopia server per integration.
- A complete failure (no snapshot saved) is only known from the task list of
  the server, lost when it restarts.
- The integration does not restore, delete or edit snapshots or policies: it
  watches them, and starts them if allowed.
- Not affiliated with Kopia. Report a problem or an idea on
  [the issues](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-kopia/issues).

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Kopia asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Kopia server | `section` | No | Kopia started as a server with its web interface (kopia server start). Enter its address, its username and its password, then add the sources to follow from the Discover tab. |
| Kopia address | `string` | Yes | The address of the web interface, port 51515 by default. https:\/\/ if the server uses TLS. |
| Username | `string` | No | The --server-username of the server, kopia by default. |
| Password | `secret` | Yes | The --server-password of the server (not the password of the repository). |
| Certificate fingerprint | `string` | No | Only for a self-signed certificate (--tls-generate-cert): its SHA-256 fingerprint, shown by Kopia at startup (SERVER CERT SHA256). Empty otherwise. |
| Options | `section` | No |  |
| Refresh interval | `select` | No | How often Kopia is read. Every 30 seconds while a snapshot runs. |
| Overdue after | `select` | No | A source without a successful snapshot for this long is overdue. Automatic: its scheduling interval plus a margin; a source without interval is then never overdue. |
| Allow starting snapshots | `boolean` | No | Lets the scene action "Start a snapshot" start a snapshot in Kopia. |
| Language of the names | `select` | No | Language of the feature names (set when a device is added), of the states and of the scene results. |

## How to install Kopia in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Kopia appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-kopia:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-kopia](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-kopia).

Kopia requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Kopia is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
